paragraphs: Yitzḥak, the son of Rav Yehudah bar Yeḥezkel, Midrash Ḥazit, at the first verse. In parashat Naso, chapter 14, however, 'R. Yaakov bar Rav Yehudah' is a scribal error. Rav Yehudah bar (or bar Rav) Yitzḥak may be his son. His father Rav Yehudah sent him to see how Ulla recited havdalah, but he sent Abaye. His father became angry with him and said, 'The master's lordship and the master's grandeur have caused the master not to transmit a teaching from his mouth,' Arvei Pesaḥim (104b). Ulla saw that Rav Yitzḥak had grown up and had not married, Kiddushin (71b). And Rav Aḥa bar Rav Huna, Rav Shemuel bar bar Ḥana, Rabbah, and Rav Kahana (see his entry). And Rav Huna, Rabbah bar Rav Huna, and Rami bar Shemuel (see his entry). Yalta, Rav Naḥman’s wife, brought a blood sample before Yitzḥak and before Rabbah bar bar Ḥana (see his entry). And Rav Kahana. Ulla (see above). Rava bar Ittai, Shevuot (37a). Rabbah (see above). Rabbah bar bar Ḥana (see above). He used to be before Rami bar Ḥama, left him, and came before Rav Sheshet. Rami said to him, ‘A duke took me by the hand. Did his scent rub off on it?’ [following Rashi’s explanation of the proverb], Zevaḥim (96b); see there. Rami bar Shemuel (see above). Rav Shemuel bar bar Ḥana (see above). Rav Sheshet (see above). Rav Pappa was serving drinks at Abba Mar's wedding; he raised a cup to R. Yitzḥak bar Rav Yehudah, who did not stand before him, and he took offense. This is our present reading. Yuḥasin, however, writes: R. Yitzḥak, Rav Pappa's student, at the wedding (see above, Rav Pappa, where Yuḥasin is correct).
